@common.sizeUnit.byte.sameAsSourceJustification: Dutch uses the same word and plural: macOS Finder nl SP27/SP28 render byte / bytes.

@common.sizeUnit.kibibyte.sameAsSourceJustification: Dutch keeps the IEC binary symbols as written (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB): KDE Dolphin nl renders the MiB suffix as MiB (dolphin.po), and IEC 80000-13 symbols are international.

@common.sizeUnit.mebibyte.sameAsSourceJustification: Dutch keeps the IEC binary symbols as written (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB): KDE Dolphin nl renders the MiB suffix as MiB (dolphin.po), and IEC 80000-13 symbols are international.

@common.sizeUnit.gibibyte.sameAsSourceJustification: Dutch keeps the IEC binary symbols as written (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB): KDE Dolphin nl renders the MiB suffix as MiB (dolphin.po), and IEC 80000-13 symbols are international.

@common.sizeUnit.kilobyte.sameAsSourceJustification: Dutch writes the SI symbol kB as English does (lowercase k is the SI prefix): GNOME/KDE nl write kB (4 kB/s), and macOS Finder nl keeps the decimal MB/GB symbols unchanged.

@common.sizeUnit.megabyte.sameAsSourceJustification: Dutch macOS Finder writes the same unit symbols (nl Finder SP24–SP26: GB, MB, KB); SI symbols are international, so Dutch keeps them as English does.
